content:
The spiritual combat is the struggle that every Christian must wage against the enemies of the soul: the devil, the world, and our own disordered passions. Victory in this combat does not consist in never feeling temptation, but in never consenting to it.

Distrust of self is the first weapon. We must be convinced that of ourselves we can do nothing, and that every good thought, every victory over sin, comes from the grace of God. Those who trust in their own strength fall; those who distrust themselves and rely on God stand firm.

Confidence in God is the second weapon. He is more desirous of our salvation than we are ourselves. He never permits us to be tempted beyond our strength, and with every temptation He provides the means of escape. Call upon Him at the first sign of danger.

The third weapon is the right use of the faculties of the soul. The understanding must be occupied with the truths of faith; the will must be fixed on the love of God; the memory must recall the benefits of God and the examples of the saints. By these means the soul is strengthened for the combat.

Finally, prayer is indispensable. Without it we fight unarmed. Ask continually for the grace to know your weakness, to distrust yourself, and to place all your confidence in God alone.
